Executive Order 13536 of 2010-04-12 (75 FR 19869, PDF pages 1-4) is held as the Federal Register original (govinfo PDF text layer, grade official original). I read it in full and confirm its identity and its clause inventory of 26 scopes as prepared (a dup2 suffix distinguishes repeated item labels in different subsections). Its authority is IEEPA, the NEA and the other statutes it names, and it rests on the national emergency with respect to Somalia declared in the lead clause of Executive Order 13536 on April 12, 2010 (as to which the measures adopted on that date and on July 20, 2012 were continued). Notice of April 8, 2026 (91 FR 18765; FR Doc. 2026-07069) states that the emergency must continue in effect beyond April 12, 2026, so the emergency, and the order that depends on it, were in effect on the cutoff of 2026-10-14 (NEA section 202(d)). Earlier annual continuation notices for the same emergency are also held; the latest one is relied on because it speaks as of its date. The held original has no own-terms end, expiry or sunset. I read the coverage notes of current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point through 2026-10-09), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog (checked 2026-11-25); they show no revocation, supersession or partial revocation of this order. The Federal Register disposition notes for this order contain two entries: EO 13620 of July 20, 2012 (listed as a later event on the clauses it amended) and the Notice of April 8, 2026 (the continuation notice relied on). The only later textual change found is Executive Order 13620 section 1(a), recorded as a later event with before and after text on the five clauses it rewrote. The dossier gaps listed as NOTICE identities absent from the census are annual continuation notices and cross-references, not events that change this order; the current-law pointer gaps concern CFR and Code pointers that this claim does not rely on, because the conclusion rests on the order's own text and the continuation notice. The acting-text lead for Executive Order 14294 (Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations, May 9, 2025) was checked: a scan of the held corpus found no mention of this order in its text, so no provision targeting this order was located. The Federal Register notice FR Doc. 2026-00596 terminating the Temporary Protected Status designation of Somalia, held among the acting texts, mentions this order only in recounting its findings and does not affect it.
